title: Credential Dumping and Compromised Identity Response Playbook
source: MITRE ATT&CK T1003 / T1078 & CISA Identity and Access Management Guidance
content:
### 1. OVERVIEW & DETECTION
Credential theft involves harvesting plaintext passwords, NTLM password hashes, Kerberos tickets, or session tokens from operating system memory (LSASS process), disk credential stores (SAM registry hive, NTDS.dit), or web browser credential databases. Detection indicators include:
- Unauthorized processes requesting handle access to lsass.exe with PROCESS_VM_READ or PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS rights (Sysmon Event ID 10).
- Suspicious execution of credential dumping utilities (e.g., mimikatz, procdump.exe -ma lsass.exe, comsvcs.dll MiniDump exports, sekurlsa, secretsdump.py, rundll32.exe).
- Unauthorized volume shadow copy access or direct file reads targeting %SystemRoot%\System32\config\SAM, SYSTEM, or SECURITY registry hives.
- Anomalous Kerberos ticket requests (Event ID 4768 / 4769) exhibiting RC4 encryption (Ticket Encryption Type 0x17) characteristic of Kerberoasting attacks.
- Identity provider alerts for impossible travel, unfamiliar ASN/location logins, or MFA fatigue spamming.

### 2. EVIDENCE & ARTIFACTS TO EXAMINE
- Windows Security Event Logs: Event ID 4624 (Successful Logon with Logon Type 9/NewCredentials or Type 3/Network), Event ID 4625 (Failed Logon), Event ID 4672 (Special Privileges Assigned to New Logon).
- Sysmon Process & Access Logs: Sysmon Event ID 10 (ProcessAccess to lsass.exe with granted access masks 0x1010 or 0x1fffff), Sysmon Event ID 1 (Process Creation examining command-line arguments for procdump, taskmgr dump, or comsvcs.dll invocations).
- Active Directory Audit Logs: Event ID 4769 (Kerberos Service Ticket Request targeting high-privilege SPNs with weak RC4 ciphers), Event ID 4662 (Operation performed on Directory Object / DCSync rights replication abuse).
- Cloud Identity Logs: Microsoft Entra ID / Okta sign-in logs, Conditional Access policy evaluations, risk score evaluations, and session token issuance timestamps.

### 3. INVESTIGATION & TRIAGE
- Determine Access Level: Identify whether local administrative credentials or enterprise domain administrator credentials were exposed or dumped.
- Assess Lateral Movement: Search across enterprise endpoints for logon events (Event ID 4624) originating from the compromised machine using the harvested account credentials.
- Golden/Silver Ticket Assessment: If the KRBTGT account or machine account passwords were breached, assume attackers can forge arbitrary Kerberos tickets.

### 4. CONTAINMENT PROCEDURES
- Isolate Dumping Host: Immediately disconnect the host where LSASS memory access or SAM dumping occurred to halt further harvesting and network propagation.
- Account Quarantine & Password Reset: Force an immediate password change and smart card / MFA re-enrollment for all accounts that were logged into the compromised host during or prior to the dump.
- Invalidate Active Sessions: Revoke all active refresh tokens, OAuth grants, and Kerberos TGTs for compromised identities.
- KRBTGT Double Reset: If domain controller compromise or DCSync replication occurred, perform a coordinated two-step reset of the Active Directory KRBTGT account password.

### 5. ERADICATION, RECOVERY & REMEDIATION
- Enable LSA Protection & Credential Guard: Enforce Windows RunAsPPL (Protected Process Light) for lsass.exe and enable Windows Defender Credential Guard (Virtualization-Based Security / VBS).
- Restrict Local Administrator Re-use: Implement Microsoft LAPS (Local Administrator Password Solution) to enforce unique, auto-rotating passwords across all endpoints, eliminating Pass-the-Hash lateral movement.
- Disable Obsolete Protocols: Disable NTLMv1 and LM protocols across the domain; enforce AES-128/256 for Kerberos encryption and decommission RC4 ciphers.
- Tiered Administration Model: Enforce strict tiering where domain administrator credentials are never entered on Tier 1 (servers) or Tier 2 (workstations) systems.
